logline: Two genius hikikomori step-siblings, undefeated in every game ever played, are transported to a world called Disboard where all conflicts are settled by games - and set out to conquer all sixteen intelligent races and dethrone the god who runs the place.

renewal.note: The 12-episode anime adaptation concluded June 2014 and has not received a continuation series. A prequel film, No Game No Life: Zero, was released in July 2017. A second season has been announced and cancelled multiple times; as of 2026 no production has been confirmed.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 7.5 and Anime News Network B grade reflect a visually inventive isekai that critics found entertaining but narratively shallow; ANN noted 'it's never a question of whether the duo will win, but how'.

pull_quotes.text: It's never a question of whether Shiro and Sora will win, but how.

seasons.review_body: Madhouse adapted Yuu Kamiya's light novel series for the spring 2014 season, airing on AT-X and Tokyo MX. Anime News Network reviewer Carl Kimlinger graded it B, identifying the game-as-conflict mechanic as the show's genuine strength and the character appeal as its primary hook - noting that the absence of stakes (Sora and Shiro's victory is a foregone conclusion) is both a structural limitation and a feature, making each episode a puzzle to solve rather than a narrative to follow. The series' hyper-saturated visual palette drew consistent notice from critics as a deliberate aesthetic choice. IMDb audiences settled at 7.5.

episode_reviews.title: Beginner
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the Blank mythology and gets Sora and Shiro to Disboard within a single episode. The chess match against Tet is a confident opening.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sora accepts Tet's chess challenge from what appears to be a dying world - the moment the show's central appeal snaps into focus.
